answer: In an agent market coordinating sparrow surveys and oasis irrigation, each identity must lock collateral for 30 days. At dawn, the market allocates access to paid jobs in proportion to locked funds, with no free allowance per account. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities earns no more access than keeping it in one. To capture half the job capacity, an attacker must lock as much capital as all honest agents combined, losing its use elsewhere.
